ShouldFlashOnPlayer.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShouldFlashOnPlayer / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars' display side / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

IsUsedUp.rationale: `IsUsedUp => HasItemBeenBought` (MawBank.cs:23) is mirrored exactly. It is a live read, not display: Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:132) excludes used-up relics from the trade events, so a spent Maw Bank stops being tradable on both sides.

AfterRoomEntered.maps_to: after_room_entered (maw_bank.py:32-34), dispatched once per map-point entry from RunState.enter_point (run.py:980-983)
AfterRoomEntered.rationale: MawBank.cs:43-50 grants GoldVar(12) when `RunState.BaseRoom == room && !HasItemBeenBought`. Both clauses check out -- the flag clause is mirrored at maw_bank.py:33 and the BaseRoom clause is guard N1's subject. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-maw-bank): three room entries give +12 each (99 -> 111 -> 123 -> 135), and a fourth after a purchase gives nothing.

AfterItemPurchased.rationale: All three of MawBank.cs:52-69's early returns are accounted for: `player != base.Owner` is single-player-structural, `HasItemBeenBought` and `goldSpent <= 0` are mirrored verbatim at maw_bank.py:37. EXECUTED: a 0-gold purchase leaves the flag False and a 100-gold purchase sets it and flips is_used_up. The `base.Status = RelicStatus.Disabled` side effect of the property setter (MawBank.cs:36-39) is presentation.

guards.what: N1: `base.Owner.RunState.BaseRoom == room` (MawBank.cs:45) -- the base of the ROOM STACK, not the current room -- has no explicit counterpart in the port
guards.rationale: This is the guard that stops Maw Bank paying twice for one map point. IRunState documents the distinction precisely (IRunState.cs:98-116): CurrentRoom is the LAST room entered at the current map point and BaseRoom is the FIRST, and they differ 'like at an event where one of the options starts a combat'; RunState.BaseRoom is `_currentRooms.FirstOrDefault()` (RunState.cs:185), and the stack is cleared to one room on every travel. So `BaseRoom == room` is true exactly once per map point. The sim satisfies it STRUCTURALLY rather than by porting it: after_room_entered has exactly ONE dispatch site (`grep -c` over run.py: 1 hit, run.py:983) and it sits in enter_point, immediately after the total_floor increment (run.py:976), so it fires once per map point and never for a nested room -- a ported event that starts a combat does not re-enter a point. Recorded as a guard rather than left implicit because the equivalence is a property of the sim's room model, not of maw_bank.py, so a future nested-room dispatch would break it silently. Rule 7: leans on run.py and IRunState.cs/RunState.cs, none hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `HasItemBeenBought` is a [SavedProperty] carrying RUN-level state (MawBank.cs:25-41); the sim keeps it as an instance field set in __init__ (maw_bank.py:24-26) and never resets it
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 13 and sweep A's whole subject is a mid-combat field the sim fails to reset. Traced deliberately and this is the OPPOSITE case: the flag is meant to persist for the whole run on both sides -- C# marks it [SavedProperty] so it survives a save/load, and MawBank has no BeforeCombatStart or AfterCombatEnd override at all, so there is no C# reset for the sim to have dropped. Sim relic instances live on RunState.relics, which is exactly the lifetime required. maw_bank appears in NO sweep-A bucket (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset`), consistent with that reading.

12 is the pinned non-ascension value: there is no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension call anywhere in MawBank.cs, and `.BaseValue` bypasses any hook modification of the var. Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 19 (a port whose docstring cites the C# expression but pins the wrong number): the port's comment names `CanonicalVars: GoldVar(12)` and the source really is GoldVar(12).

run.gain_gold (run.py:325-333) runs the Hook.ModifyGoldGained chain over every relic first, truncates toward zero and no-ops on a non-positive amount, matching PlayerCmd.GainGold. Checked because it is the interaction point with Ectoplasm (which zeroes gold gains) -- Maw Bank's payout goes through the chain on both sides rather than around it.

guards.what: N5: the `goldSpent` the sim reports for a cost-ignored purchase
guards.rationale: shop.py:180 passes `gold_spent = 0 if ignore_cost else self.cost`, so Lord's Parasol's free sweep of the inventory does NOT spend Maw Bank's charge -- and MawBank.cs:62-65's `goldSpent <= 0` return is exactly that behaviour in C#, where OnTryPurchaseWrapper's ignoreCost path likewise reports no gold spent. Recorded because it is the one caller where the two could plausibly have diverged, and it is the reason the sim's port needs the `gold_spent <= 0` clause it has.
